Most bowel cancers develop from small growths of abnormal cells on the lining of the bowel called polyps.

Because polyps and bowel cancers are slow growing so if they can be detected through screening tests and

removed early, then the disease is highly treatable.

The easiest screening test is the Faecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT). (cree oh ps and cancers bl bleed

A more precise but more invasive test is a colonoscopy which is recommended every 5to10 years over the
age of 40. During a colonoscopy a flexible tube containin, rrall.camera is inserted ‘into the back passage

to look for polyps on the wall of the bowel. Patients are sedated tolavoid discomfort and any polyps are
easily removed during this procedure. Regular colonoscopiés can reduce bowel cancer mortality by about
70%.
